# Satipaṭṭhānakathā (Kv 1.9)

**ID:** Kv 1.9

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Satipaṭṭhānakathā* (Kv 1.9) is a debate located in the first chapter (*vaggasaṅgaha*) of the *Kathāvatthu*, the fifth book of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka, spanning pages 155–159 of the Pali Text Society edition [Anālayo 2006]. In addition to this debate in the *Kathāvatthu*, another exposition bearing the title *Satipaṭṭhānakathā* is found in the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Paṭis II 232–235) [Anālayo 2006; Anālayo 2010]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in one language [SuttaCentral].

SuttaCentral notes connections or cross-references between Kv 1.9 and major early discourses on mindfulness and related teachings, including the *Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta* (DN 22 and MN 10), the *Ambapālisutta* (SN 47.1), the *Cakkavattisutta* (SN 46.42), AN 1.616, the *Anumānapañha* of the *Milindapañha* (Mil 6.4.1), as well as Chinese Āgama parallels such as EA 39.7, MA 58, SĀ 721–722, and the *Lúnwáng qībǎo jīng* (T 38) [SuttaCentral].

DharmaNexus detects extensive Pali-internal text reuse (917 matches across 68 Pali texts), sharing significant textual passages with the *Satipaṭṭhāna Saṁyutta* (SN 47), the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, other *Kathāvatthu* chapters including *Rūpaṁkammantikathā* (Kv 8.9) and *Puggalakathā* (Kv 1.1), the *Pañcakanipāta* (AN 5), *Chakkanipāta* (AN 6), *Bojjhaṅga Saṁyutta* (SN 46), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*'s *Rūpavibhatti* (Ds 2.2.3), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Visuddhimagga* [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language automated alignments, DharmaNexus detects textual matches with Chinese canonical texts—including the *Zá āhán jīng* (T 99), the *Zhōng āhán jīng* (T 26), the *Zēngyī āhán jīng* (T 125), and T 38 (where DharmaNexus agrees with SuttaCentral)—as well as Sanskrit texts like the *Pañcaviṃśatisāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* and Tibetan canonical works such as the *Kāraṇaprajñapti* (D4087) and *Abhidharmakośaṭīkā* (D4092) [DharmaNexus].
